notes: §1985:VII.3.4.2 prints CODE-SET IS alphabet-name-1, CODE-SET the one underlined word. codeSetClause's first alternative is CODE_SET IS? cobolWord cobolWord? and its second the FOR ALPHANUMERIC / FOR NATIONAL phrases (codeSetForPhrase); the 1985 edition reaches its one-name format through VisitCodeSetClause, which refuses a second alphabet-name and either FOR phrase at --std 85 (COBOL0900, the 2002 two-class format), and BindCodeSetClause resolves alphabet-name-1 against the SPECIAL-NAMES ALPHABET clauses and binds the conversion to the file. FileDescriptionClauseAdmitted keeps the clause to a sequential file and ScreenClauseRepetition to one occurrence. Probed at 85: CODE-SET IS ASC and CODE-SET ASC compile; a file under CODE-SET IS EBC (ALPHABET EBC IS EBCDIC) is written in EBCDIC on the medium (HELLO is C8 C5 D3 D3 D6) and reads back HELLO; CODE-SET IS ASC NAT, CODE-SET FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS ASC and CODE-SET ALPHANUMERIC ASC (COBOL0900), CODE-SET IS with no name, a literal, STANDARD-1 or NATIVE written directly, CODE-SET ARE and CODE SET (syntax errors), a data-name, a class-name or an undefined word as the operand (COBOL5985), the clause twice (COBOL2423), on a relative file (COBOL2604) and in an SD (COBOL1970) are refused. The witness declares ALPHABET ASC IS STANDARD-1, writes one record under CODE-SET IS ASC and reads it back.

next.reason: §1985:VII.3.4.2 is 'CODE-SET IS alphabet-name-1' alone. §2023:13.18.13.2 keeps that form but adds an optional alphabet-name-2 (a national alphabet) and the 'FOR ALPHANUMERIC' / 'FOR NATIONAL' phrases, and the sequential file description entry §2023:13.4.5.2 'Format 1 (sequential)' restates the same wider clause in line. A 1985 CODE-SET clause means the same, but programs the 1985 format refuses are accepted: CHANGED. The USAGE DISPLAY and SIGN SEPARATE restriction (§1985:VII.3.4.3 SR1, carried by §2023:13.18.13.3 SR3) is that rule's own record.
